name: NSE: the Gateway Router's TLS leg, and GR_REQUEST/GR_RESPONSE

steps.comment: The Gateway Router is the ONLY TLS hop in NSE's connection sequence -- the member dials it (here, port 9022) under TLS to collect a session key and a fresh AES-256-GCM key/IV, then opens the gateway itself (port 9021, scenario 17) over plain TCP with that encryption layered above it, exactly as published. 35=transaction code, 9004=ErrorCode, 9170=BoxId, 9120=BrokerId, 9171=IpAddress, 9172=Port.

GR_REQUEST (2400) for box 3, entitled to broker 10199. Box 3 carries no users and is not dialled at the gateway by any other scenario: a box that collects secrets here encrypts every message from SECURE_BOX_REGISTRATION_REQUEST onward for the rest of the daemon's life, so reusing box 1 or 2 (which 17/18/19 sign on to in the clear) would silently break them the next time this daemon runs those scenarios.

GR_RESPONSE (2401), error 0. Asserting the shape only: error code, the box id echoed back, and the gateway's port (9021, from config -- stable, not something the exchange assigns per run). The session key and the four cryptographic fields are fresh random bytes on every call and are deliberately not asserted on.

The router answers one request and closes the connection (close_when_flushed). Drop it explicitly so the next 'send' opens a fresh TLS handshake rather than writing to a socket the peer has already closed.
A Box ID nothing in config/nse.json configures. 16588 is USER_IP_REC_NOT_FOUND.
Box 3 again, but with a broker it is not entitled to. 16041 is INVALID_BROKER_OR_BRANCH.
